title: Nagi Bird Sanctuary
tagline: Nagi Bird Sanctuary — Bihar’s Ramsar Wetland Jewel & Migratory Avian Haven

heroImage.alt: Nagi Bird Sanctuary - One of the views from the dam wall

overview.short: Nagi Bird Sanctuary (and adjacent Nakti Dam) in Jamui spans 7.91 square kilometers of crystal-clear reservoir waters, designated as Ramsar Wetlands in 2024.
overview.description: Surrounded by the scenic hills and dry deciduous Sal forests of Jamui district, Nagi Dam was created for irrigation and has evolved into one of Eastern India’s richest waterfowl refuges. Recognized as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2024, it hosts over 20,000 migratory birds each winter, including the Bar-headed Goose (over 1.6% of the global population), painted storks, red-crested pochards, and osprey.
features: Host to 1.6% of Global Bar-headed Goose Population
Host Venue of Bihar’s State Bird Festival "Kalrav"
overview.about: A scenic avian paradise where azure reservoir waters, misty winter hillocks, and thousands of Bar-headed Geese greet nature lovers.

howToReach.roadNote: Located 15 km from Jhajha and 35 km from Jamui town via SH-18 and local paved roads.
